Mala Dobron Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mala Dobron, Ukraine

Not demolished. This cemetery existed by 1855 per its oldest tombstone, used until WWII, with one exceptional postwar burial in 1973. Jews are believed to have arrived in the early 19th century; population reached 15 by 1830 and 182 (17%) by 1880, remaining stable through the 1921 Czechoslovak period. Jews earned livelihoods through farming and managing the town's mineral baths. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; population fell to 139 by 1941, when area Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled that August to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered. The remaining 140 Mala Dobron Jews were deported to Auschwitz in mid-May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
